title: Contingency signal grid and owner checkrun
body:
Purpose
This is a working doc for the upcoming feature launch (feature flag: smart-routing-v2). It consolidates the contingency signals we will watch during ramp, maps each signal to a primary and secondary owner, and outlines immediate runbook steps and rollback criteria. Intended for product-ops, SRE, and the launch on-call rotation.

Notes to self / context
- This is intentionally concise; link to long-form runbook in Confluence (CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-RUNBOOK-21).
- Target launch window: Nov 17–21, 2025 (phased ramp). Canary starts at 0.5% of traffic.
- Primary goal: detect service-quality regressions linked to model routing changes quickly and minimize business impact.

Quick summary (one-liner)
If any of the high-severity signals breach the defined guardrails during canary or staged ramp, page the primary owner and execute the corresponding immediate mitigation. If mitigation fails or signal persists for >15 minutes, fallback and begin rollback plan.

Signal grid (severity-based)
- SEV 1: End-to-end error rate (5m rolling) > 1% absolute increase vs baseline AND user-facing 503/500 spike in production routes.
  - Primary owner: SRE on-call (Liam O'Connor)
  - Secondary owner: Serving runtime lead (Jasper Kim)
  - Immediate runbook step: increase rate limit and divert canary traffic to fallback model variant; toggle canary flag to 0% if errors persist >2 minutes after mitigation.
  - KPI impact: direct drop in success rate; monitor failed requests per minute and timer-based SLO breaches.
  - Escalation: page engineering manager + product manager if persists >15 minutes.

- SEV 1b: Latency tail (p95) for generation API > 200ms above baseline for 3 consecutive minutes during canary
  - Primary owner: Serving runtime (Jasper Kim)
  - Secondary owner: SRE (Ethan Morales)
  - Immediate runbook: switch canary traffic to lower-capacity model quantization profile; invoke autoscale target increase for dedicated pool; if no improvement in 5m, cut canary to 0%.

- SEV 2: Cost per 1k tokens increases > 25% vs forecasted for canary traffic (sustained 10m)
  - Primary owner: Product ops (Maya Chen)
  - Secondary owner: Finance ops (Priya Nair)
  - Immediate runbook: pause non-essential background jobs that may use models; enable per-route cost-caps; consider throttling low-priority customers; notify go-to-market for possible billing adjustments.

- SEV 3: Quality regression detected by eval set (automated quality monitor) — significant drop in BLEU/QA metrics or user-reported regressions > threshold
  - Primary owner: Applied ML lead (Priya Nair)
  - Secondary owner: Product Manager (assigned PM)
  - Immediate runbook: run the diff-eval harness (ref: CONFLUENCE-EVAL-43); quarantine the model variant; revert to previous verified model rollout for affected segments.

Metric watchlist (live dashboards to open)
- Token-level cost by route (token-cost-dashboard)
- Error-rate heatmap (per-region, per-model)
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) by variant
- Models-in-use: KV-cache hit rate
- Canary adoption % and user conversion funnel (if experiment enabled)

Canary / staged ramp criteria (pass/fail gates)
- Gate 1 (0 -> 0.5% traffic): no SEV1s; error rate within +0.2% of baseline; p95 latency within +50ms; cost delta < 5% sustained 10m.
- Gate 2 (0.5 -> 5%): no SEV1s in 30m window; error rate within +0.5%; p95 within +100ms; sign-off from SRE and PM.
- Gate 3 (5 -> 25%): no SEV1s in 60m window; quality evals within tolerance; cost delta < 15%; PM + Eng release lead approve.
- Gate 4 (25 -> 100%): rolling checks every 30m for first 6h, then hourly. Any SEV1 triggers rollback.

Owner responsibilities (plain language)
- Primary owner: own immediate mitigation and coordinate with secondary; update the incident slack channel with every significant action and time-stamp (eg. #launch-smart-routing).
- Secondary owner: prepare to take ownership if primary is not reachable in 5 minutes; run fallback toggles if primary is executing other mitigation steps.
- Product-Ops: keep stakeholder matrix updated (email cadence), manage postmortem ownership, and track cost/KPI impact in the ramp tracker sheet.

Runbook snippets (cut-and-paste quick actions)
- Toggle canary to 0%: infra console -> feature-flags -> smart-routing-v2 -> set percentage = 0 -> confirm. Notify SRE and PM in channel.
- Divert to fallback model: infra -> routing -> model-variant-bind -> set route to model-v1-fallback -> confirm success on a small sample traffic.
- Enable autoscale target bump: infra -> dedicated-clusters -> edit autoscale -> +30% target -> monitor GPU utilization.
- Throttle background jobs: scheduler -> pause job group "async-annotations" -> verify token usage drops.

Prelaunch checklist (must be green before Gate 1)
- Instrumentation: dashboards created and shared (owner: SRE) -> checklist: token-cost dashboard, error heatmap, latency percentiles, kv-cache monitor.
- Alerts: alert rules created + escalation path tested (owner: SRE) -> test page and confirm pages within 5 minutes.
- Rollback button validated in staging and prod (owner: infra PM).
- Canary flag toggles tested and rollback time measured (should be < 90s end-to-end).
- Cost-safeguards: per-route cost caps configured for canary routes.
- Eval harness: automated tests run nightly for the canary model; baseline stored (owner: applied-ml).
- Stakeholder comms: stakeholders list + 15-min status cadence during ramp (owner: product-ops).

Communication plan during ramp
- Slack channel: #launch-smart-routing (all owners + exec watchlist)
- 15-minute updates during first 90 minutes (product-ops posts): current canary %, top signal deltas, actions taken, next checkpoint time.
- Escalation to Exec (email and SMS) if SEV1 persists >30 minutes or if cost impact forecasted > $5k over baseline in first 24h.

Postmortem template (quick fields)
- Summary (what happened)
- Timeline (minute-level)
- Signal(s) that tripped
- Actions taken and timestamps
- Root cause (if known)
- Mitigation and long-term fix owners + ETA
- Learnings and playbook updates

Open questions / TODOs (notes, not blockers unless noted)
- Confirm exact canary percent caps for specific customer segments (PM + sales input).
- Validate rollback latency for stateful sessions (SRE). Current estimate is ~45–70s; need hard test.
- Decide whether to add automated rollback after 3 consecutive SEV1 pings (product decision).
- Add scenario: cloud-region-specific fallback (APAC region has different capacity constraints).

Useful links and references
- CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-RUNBOOK-21 (main runbook)
- CONFLUENCE-EVAL-43 (diff-eval harness)
- JIRA-PRODOPS-948 (prelaunch checklist epic)
- github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1624 (canary flag automation)

Notes (scratch)
- If we observe cost >15% but no quality regressions, prefer throttling low-priority workloads before full rollback; minimizes user-facing disruption.
- Keep this doc short and feed it into the launch dashboard (product-ops will push final checklist there).

Revision history
- 2025-10-07 created by Maya Chen (initial grid + checklist)
- 2025-10-25 updated: clarified latency gates and added cost-safeguard steps (Priya)
- 2025-11-12 updated: tightened escalation timing and added autoscale bump action (Liam)

End of doc
